judgment_text:
The Order of the Court was delivered by

R. Vijayakumar, J.:— The present petition has been filed by the accused person in C.C. No. 479 of 2018, on the file of the Judicial Magistrate, Additional Mahila Court, Nagercoil, seeking to set aside the order dated 30-10-2025 passed in Cr.M.P. No. 944 of 2025 wherein an order of proclamation has been issued under Section 82 of CrPC

2. A perusal of the records reveal that the wife of the petitioner has lodged a complaint under Section 498-A, IPC, along with other provisions as against the petitioner and his family members. The petitioner had not appeared and he was absconding. Despite issuance of NBW, he could not be secured. The case was split up and the mother of the petitioner was also arrayed as an accused has been acquitted. Thereafter, a proclamation order has been passed by the Judicial Magistrate, Additional Mahila Court, Nagercoil, on 30-10-2025 invoking Section 82 of CrPC

3. According to the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner, he was working in Assam and he was not aware of the issuance of NBW as against him. He was under the impression that the case as against him has been closed. Considering the fact that one of the accused persons has already has been acquitted and the petitioner is ready to surrender before the concerned Court and face the trial, this Court is inclined to pass the following order:

(a) An order dated 30-10-2025 in Cr.M.P. No. 944 of 2025 C.C. No. 479 of 2018, on the file of the learned Judicial Magistrate, Additional Mahila Court, Nagercoil, is hereby set aside; and

(b) The petitioner is directed to surrender before the Judicial Magistrate, Additional Mahila Court, Nagercoil, on or before 6-4-2026 and on such surrender, the learned Judicial Magistrate, Additional Mahila Court, Nagercoil, is directed to consider the recall application and permit the petitioner to participate in the trial.

4. With the above said observations, this Criminal Original Petition stands allowed to the extent as stated above.
